message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"3.66","text":"And your task is to command what is necessary, while the brothers’ task is to submit and not disobey. Those who submit, then, will be saved, but those who disobey will be punished by the Messiah, because the one presiding has been entrusted with the Messiah’s place. Therefore, either honor or insult shown to the one presiding is carried to the Messiah, and from the Messiah it is referred to God. I have said this so that the brothers themselves may not be unaware of their own danger from disobedience toward you: whoever disobeys when you command disobeys the Messiah, and one who has disobeyed the Messiah provokes God to anger.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"σοῦ μὲν ἔργον ἐστὶν κελεύειν ἃ δεῖ, τῶν ἀδελφῶν ὑπείκειν","chosen":"your task is to command what is necessary, while the brothers’ task is to submit","rationale":"The second clause elides ἔργον ἐστίν, which is supplied in English without adding a new claim."},{"source_quote":"ὁ προκαθεζόμενος χριστοῦ τόπον πεπίστευται","chosen":"the one presiding has been entrusted with the Messiah’s place","rationale":"The passive πεπίστευται presents the presider as entrusted with a representative position; it does not identify him as the Messiah."},{"source_quote":"ἤτοι τιμὴ ἢ ὕβρις τοῦ προκαθεζομένου","chosen":"either honor or insult shown to the one presiding","rationale":"The genitive is understood objectively in context: the honor or insult is directed toward the presider. A less likely formal alternative is “the presider’s honor or insult.”"},{"source_quote":"χριστοῦ","chosen":"Messiah","rationale":"Χριστός functions independently as a title throughout the passage rather than as part of a personal-name construction."},{"source_quote":"τῆς πρὸς σὲ ἀπειθείας τὸν κίνδυνον αὐτῶν","chosen":"their own danger from disobedience toward you","rationale":"The placement of αὐτῶν is awkward but defensibly identifies the danger as belonging to the brothers; the genitive ἀπειθείας indicates the disobedience from which that danger arises."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"3.67","text":"The church, therefore, like a city built on a height, must have a God-loving order and good administration. Above all, let the bishop, as ruler, be listened to in the matters about which he speaks. Let the elders be diligent to see that what is commanded is done. Let the deacons, going all around among the brothers, look after their bodies and souls and confer with the bishop. Let all the other brothers accept being wronged; but if they want their cases concerning the wrongs done to them to be judged, let them be brought to agreement before the elders. The elders are then to report the settlement also to the bishop.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὡς πόλιν ἐν ὕψει ᾠκοδομημένην","chosen":"like a city built on a height","rationale":"This preserves both the city comparison and its elevated location without turning the image into a quotation from another text."},{"source_quote":"φιλόθεον ἔχειν τάξιν","chosen":"have a God-loving order","rationale":"The adjective φιλόθεον directly characterizes the community’s τάξις as devoted to or loving God."},{"source_quote":"περὶ ὧν λέγει ἀκουέσθω","chosen":"let ... be listened to in the matters about which he speaks","rationale":"The passive of ἀκούω can imply being heeded or obeyed; “be listened to” preserves that force without making obedience more explicit than the wording requires."},{"source_quote":"ἐκπεριερχόμενοί τῶν ἀδελφῶν τὰ σώματα καὶ τὰς ψυχὰς ἐπισκεπτέσθωσαν καὶ τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ ἀντιβαλλέτωσαν","chosen":"going all around among the brothers, look after their bodies and souls and confer with the bishop","rationale":"Ἐπισκέπτομαι includes visiting, inspecting, and caring for. The uncommon ἀντιβάλλω may indicate conferring with, reporting back to, or laying the findings before the bishop; “confer with” leaves the precise exchange open."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων συμβιβαζέσθωσαν","chosen":"let them be brought to agreement before the elders","rationale":"The passive or middle συμβιβάζεσθαι can denote reconciliation or the settlement of a dispute; the following συμβιβασμόν supports an agreed settlement."},{"source_quote":"τὸν δὲ συμβιβασμὸν ... τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ προσαναφερέτωσαν","chosen":"report the settlement also to the bishop","rationale":"Προσαναφέρω here denotes referring or reporting the elders’ settlement upward or additionally to the bishop."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"3.68","text":"Let them expedite the marriages not only of the young but also of those advanced in years, lest seething desire bring a plague upon the church through an occasion of sexual immorality or adultery. For above every sin, the impiety of adultery is hated by God, because it destroys not only the sinner himself but also those who share his table and strive alongside him. It resembles rabies, for by nature it imparts its own madness. For chastity’s sake, therefore, let not only the elders but everyone be eager to complete marriages. The sin of the adulterer forces its way upon everyone. Therefore, urging the brothers to live chastely is the first act of mercy, for it is care for the soul; food for the body is relief.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"κατεπειγέτωσαν τοὺς γάμους","chosen":"let them expedite the marriages","rationale":"The verb calls for actively hastening the marriages rather than merely recommending them."},{"source_quote":"τῶν προβεβηκότων","chosen":"those advanced in years","rationale":"The perfect participle describes people who have progressed in age; “older people” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"προφάσει πορνείας ἢ μοιχείας","chosen":"through an occasion of sexual immorality or adultery","rationale":"Πρόφασις can mean pretext, occasion, or ostensible cause. “Through an occasion” best fits the warning that seething desire may bring the stated plague; a more literal but less clear alternative is “under a pretext of sexual immorality or adultery.”"},{"source_quote":"τοὺς συνεστιωμένους καὶ συναμιλλωμένους","chosen":"those who share his table and strive alongside him","rationale":"The two participles depict people dining with the offender and engaging alongside him. The second can also be understood more generally as associating or sharing his pursuits."},{"source_quote":"λύσσῃ γὰρ ἔοικεν","chosen":"It resembles rabies","rationale":"Λύσσα can denote rabies or raging madness; the following image of contagious madness supports the disease sense while retaining its association with frenzy."},{"source_quote":"τὸ οὖν σπεύδειν σωφρονεῖν τοὺς ἀδελφούς","chosen":"urging the brothers to live chastely","rationale":"Σπεύδειν is taken transitively as hastening or urging the brothers toward σωφροσύνη. The syntax also permits “the brothers’ being eager to live chastely.”"},{"source_quote":"ψυχῆς γὰρ ἐστὶν θεραπεία","chosen":"for it is care for the soul","rationale":"Θεραπεία can mean care, treatment, or healing; “care” preserves the contrast with bodily nourishment without asserting a specific medical image."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἀλλὰ-καὶ","issue":"The selected print joins the two particles with a hyphen. This is an orthographic or editorial feature and does not alter the ordinary construction “but also.”","proposed_reading":"ἀλλὰ καὶ","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"τοῦτο πρώτῃ ἐλεημοσύνη","issue":"The dative πρώτῃ does not agree with the predicate noun ἐλεημοσύνη. The intended predicate sense is nevertheless clear, and the translation represents it as “the first act of mercy.”","proposed_reading":"τοῦτο πρώτη ἐλεημοσύνη","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.69","text":"Nevertheless, if you love your brothers, you will take nothing away from them, but you will share what you have. You will feed the hungry, provide drink for the thirsty, clothe the naked, visit the sick, help those in prisons as far as possible, eagerly welcome strangers into your own lodgings, and hate no one. As for how you must act devoutly, your own understanding will teach you, since you are discerning. Above all—even if it is necessary to tell you—meet together more frequently; would that it were every hour, but at least on the customary days of assembly. For if you do this, you are within walls of refuge, since desertion from the ranks is the beginning of destruction. Accordingly, let no one be absent from meeting together on the pretext of petty resentment toward a brother. For if anyone among you is absent from gathering, that person will be counted among those who scatter the Messiah’s church and will be punished as one who has become one of those opposed to the Messiah’s disciples. That person will be cast out with adulterers. For, like an adulterer, he has separated himself on some pretext under the influence of the spirit within him, and has given the evil one room against himself to seize a sheep as one found outside the folds.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"οὐδὲν αὐτῶν ἀφαιρήσεσθε","chosen":"you will take nothing away from them","rationale":"The middle form can mean taking something from others for oneself or depriving them; the following promise to share one’s possessions supplies the contrast."},{"source_quote":"εὐγνωμονοῦντας ὑμᾶς","chosen":"since you are discerning","rationale":"Εὐγνωμονέω can describe being sensible, fair-minded, or well-disposed. Here it concerns the readers’ capacity to recognize how piety should be practiced."},{"source_quote":"ἐντὸς τειχῶν ἀσυλίας ἐστέ","chosen":"you are within walls of refuge","rationale":"The rendering preserves the enclosing-wall image and takes ἀσυλία as safety, immunity, or inviolable refuge."},{"source_quote":"ἀρχὴ γὰρ ἀπωλείας λειποταξία","chosen":"desertion from the ranks is the beginning of destruction","rationale":"Λειποταξία is a military term for abandoning one’s assigned position, here applied metaphorically to absence from the assembly."},{"source_quote":"προφάσει μικροψυχίας τῆς πρὸς ἀδελφὸν","chosen":"on the pretext of petty resentment toward a brother","rationale":"Μικροψυχία literally suggests smallness or faintness of spirit and can denote pettiness or discouragement. In this interpersonal setting, “petty resentment” is contextually defensible; “discouragement concerning a brother” remains possible."},{"source_quote":"τὴν χριστοῦ ἐκκλησίαν","chosen":"the Messiah’s church","rationale":"Χριστός is used independently as a title, not within a personal-name construction."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ πνεύματος","chosen":"under the influence of the spirit within him","rationale":"The phrase identifies the spirit as the agent of his self-separation but does not explicitly identify it as his own spirit, the Holy Spirit, or an evil spirit; lowercase wording preserves that uncertainty."},{"source_quote":"πρόβατον ἁρπάσαι ὡς μανδρῶν ἔξω εὑρεθέν","chosen":"to seize a sheep as one found outside the folds","rationale":"The absent person is depicted through the sheep image. The ὡς with the participle presents the sheep as regarded or found outside, while μανδρῶν is plural, “folds.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"συνεχέστερον συνέρχεσθε, εἴθε καθ’ ὥραν, ἐπεί γε ἐν ταῖς νενομισμέναις τῆς συνόδου ἡμέραις","issue":"The wish εἴθε καθ’ ὥραν is followed by a verbless ἐπεί γε phrase. The translation treats the latter as an elliptical minimum—“but at least on the customary days of assembly.” The more formally connective alternative “since at least on the customary days of assembly” leaves the same gathering verb implicit. No missing wording has been restored.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὡς γὰρ μοιχὸς ὑπὸ τοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ πνεύματος προφάσει τινὸς ἑαυτὸν ἀφώρισεν","issue":"The opening comparison and the agent phrase permit more than one attachment: the absent person may be compared with an adulterer, or ὡς μοιχός may characterize him directly as one. The main rendering takes it as a comparison and attaches “by the spirit within him” to his self-separation.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.70","text":"However, listen to your bishop, and do not grow weary in rendering him every honor, knowing that, though ostensibly directed to him, it is carried to the Messiah; from the Messiah it is referred to God, and it is repaid many times over to the one who offered it. You will therefore honor the Messiah’s throne, since you were also commanded to honor Moses’ seat, even if those who preside are regarded as sinners. These things have been said to you sufficiently. But as for how he must live blamelessly, I consider it superfluous to speak, since he is a proven disciple of the one who taught even me.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τοῦ ἐπισκόπου ὑμῶν ἀκούετε","chosen":"listen to your bishop","rationale":"The genitive with ἀκούετε can include heeding or obeying; “listen to” preserves that range while the surrounding commands establish the authoritative setting."},{"source_quote":"προφάσει τῇ πρὸς αὐτὸν εἰς χριστὸν φέρεται","chosen":"though ostensibly directed to him, it is carried to the Messiah","rationale":"The implied subject is the honor just mentioned. Πρόφασις marks its outward or apparent direction toward the bishop, while the author says its ultimate recipient is the Messiah."},{"source_quote":"χριστὸν","chosen":"Messiah","rationale":"Χριστός functions independently as a title throughout the passage rather than as part of a personal name."},{"source_quote":"πολυπλασίως ἀνταποδίδοται","chosen":"it is repaid many times over","rationale":"The adverb indicates a multiplied return rather than merely an equivalent repayment."},{"source_quote":"θρόνον ... χριστοῦ ... Μωϋσέως καθέδραν","chosen":"the Messiah’s throne ... Moses’ seat","rationale":"Distinct English terms preserve the source’s distinction between θρόνος and καθέδρα rather than harmonizing both as “seat” or “chair.”"},{"source_quote":"δόκιμος ὑπάρχει μαθητής","chosen":"he is a proven disciple","rationale":"Δόκιμος describes someone tested and found approved or dependable; “proven” conveys that evaluative force."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ κἀμὲ διδάξαντος","chosen":"of the one who taught even me","rationale":"The crasis κἀμέ means “me also” or, with rhetorical emphasis, “even me”; the latter suits the speaker’s appeal to the bishop’s teacher."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
